title: Mitigate adaptive floodgate queue starvation across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (anonymized IDs: CUST-AF, CUST-FN) reported intermittent 5xx errors and dramatic long-context tail latency spikes during peak periods across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Investigation showed queue starvation and backlog amplification when small/short-sequence request floods coincided with long-context streaming requests.

Observed symptoms:
- 95th/99th token latencies spiking up to 5-8x baseline on affected clusters during short-request floods.
- Elevated request timeouts and 503s in Dedicated clusters with token-based quota enforcement.
- Private (VPC) customers with higher inter-node RTTs saw amplified backlog and KV-cache eviction-induced stalls.
- Correlation between traffic composition changes (sudden small-message bursts) and scheduler starvation windows.

Root cause (summary):
1) Global inflight accounting and batching admission allowed many small requests to occupy batching capacity because the scheduler's cost estimator favored request-count rather than token-cost under certain thresholds. Small requests would be continuously batched and dispatched, starving longer-context requests that rely on larger batch slots.
2) The KV-cache eviction policy had an aggressive checkpoint that, when combined with head-of-line long-context requests, triggered short-lived cache thrashing and increased per-request latency (eviction-induced stalls).
3) Private deployments with higher RTTs increased the effective service time for long requests, worsening starvation under the same admission policy.
4) Edge case: request timeouts in the Dedicated admission controller caused inflight tokens to be returned late, amplifying backlog (race between RTT/timeouts and token return).

Decisions and trade-offs:
- We prioritized a fix that preserves throughput for small-request workloads (important for PLG customers) while protecting long-context latency SLOs.
- Rejected a simple fixed quota per-request-size bucket because it reduced overall throughput in some production mixes.
- Chosen approach: adaptive, token-aware admission controller ("adaptive_floodgate") + per-tenant inflight windows + KV-cache grace window for recently used prefixes. This minimizes regressive throughput while restoring fairness.

Fix implemented (high-level):
- Adaptive Floodgate: new admission logic that uses a moving-average token cost per tenant and scales their inflight window dynamically. Short bursts see reduced immediate headroom while long-context tenants are guaranteed a minimal inflight share.
- Token-budget-aware batching: batch assembly now considers token budgets (estimated total tokens) rather than only request counts, preventing small requests from monopolizing batch slots meant for long-context requests.
- Per-tenant inflight windows: limits per-tenant concurrent tokens with fast-path relaxation for authenticated internal backfills (pre-approved).
- KV-cache grace window: short grace period for recently accessed KV-prefixes to prevent eviction during critical long-context requests; reduced unnecessary cache churn.
- Race fix: deterministic token-return path on request cancellation/timeout to ensure inflight counters free immediately.
- Feature flag: adaptive_floodgate defaulted to off, toggled on for canaries and then universally enabled after validation.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for admission logic, token accounting, and timeout handling added.
- Integration tests simulating mixed workloads (small-message floods + long-context streams) added to CI (runtime/integration/mixed_workloads_test.go).
- Large-scale soak and chaos testing in a separate staging fleet: 48-hour soak with synthetic mixes representative of customer workloads.
- Benchmarks: 95th tail for long-context scenarios improved from ~1.8s to ~320ms on the canary Dedicated cluster; error rate reduced by ~87% for impacted customers.

Deployment plan and rollout:
1) Feature gated rollout to a single Dedicated canary pool (2025-02-22). Observed metrics for 48 hours.
2) Expand to Hosted canary subset (2025-02-25) and one Private customer (CUST-AF) with explicit opt-in.
3) Full rollout to Dedicated and Hosted (runtime-1.19) on 2025-03-02 after on-call sign-off.
4) Private customers offered optional upgrade bundle; coordinating with Solutions to schedule maintenance windows.

Monitoring and instrumentation changes:
- New metrics: tenant_token_avg, tenant_inflight_window, floodgate_block_rate, kv_grace_evictions.
- Dashboards: runtime -> Scheduler -> Floodgate (link below).
- Alerts: floodgate_block_rate > 0.5% for 5m triggers paging (P0).

Customer communications and escalations:
- Notified affected customers with root cause summary and mitigations on 2025-02-24.
- Provided per-tenant metrics and timeline; temporary workarounds included manual inflight window increases for high-priority tenants.
- Follow-up call with largest affected customer (CUST-FN) on 2025-02-26; post-deploy SLA report shared.

Postmortem action items (owners):
- ENG: Tune adaptive scaling parameters and finalize heuristics (Daniel Cho).
- ENG: Add long-term simulation harness for mixed workloads to CI (Sofia Ramirez).
- PM: Update status page runbooks and internal KB for per-tenant throttling (Maya Patel).
- Design/Console: Add UI surface in Console to expose per-tenant inflight windows and floodgate status (DES/PM follow-up).

Outcome: Fix deployed in runtime-1.19 and rolled out across Hosted and Dedicated. Customers reporting restored latency SLOs; no throughput regressions observed on representative production mixes.

comments: 2025-02-18 - Sofia R: Created ticket after escalation from Support. Initial triage points to scheduling/mysql-like head-of-line behavior during small-request floods.
2025-02-19 - Daniel C: Reproduced locally with synthetic driver. Confirmed starvation when small requests >80% of mix for sustained 30s.
2025-02-20 - PR opened: runtime/pr#4829 with adaptive_floodgate prototype. Added unit tests and initial docs.
2025-02-22 - Canary deploy (Dedicated cluster d-c1). 48h observation: 95th latency down 68%, error spikes reduced. Noted one regression on a synthetic extreme throughput test (follow-up tuning).
2025-02-25 - Expanded to Hosted canaries and Private opt-in with CUST-AF. Observed consistent improvements. Engineering adjusted grace window from 150ms to 250ms after observed eviction flaps.
2025-03-02 - Full rollout to Dedicated and Hosted under runtime-1.19. No customer-facing incidents during rollout. Support communications sent.
2025-03-04 - Post-deploy: Daniel C published tuning guide and flagged next steps for metrics retention and Console UX.
